Targets: 1 Unit established • 6 Women hired and retained • @ Least 75% of reports produced by women
Six women journalists have been hired and staffing levels have been maintained throughout the project.
Equipment procured for the journalists is available in the offices and for use outside when reporting.
100% of reports have been produced by women.
Targets: 6 Women trained; 8 Interns given experience; good-quality reporting
Trainings have been conducted for the 6 female jounalists and they note that the trianings have ben useful. The trianings were held at Peace Hotel in Mogadishu. Enquiries on the usefulness and relevance of the trainings delivered under BILAN program revealed the trainings enhanced their journalism skills in producing quality stories such as filming and photography, editing, mobile journalism, reporting, interviewing and story scripting. The women journalists indicated that they feel more confident and can now work with international media houses after acquiring these new skills.
Additional remote mentoring sessions/masterclasses have been held throughout the year with household name journalists, including ITV’s Rageh Omar; the BBC’s Lyse Doucet, Mishal Hussein, Anna Holligan and Roger Wood; Channel 4’s Lindsey Hilsum and the New York Times’s Abdi Latif Dahir.
https://undpsomalia.exposure.co/lyse-doucet-masterclass-caps-6-amazing-months-for-bilan
2 interns were hired in July and will complete their 6-month placements with Bilan in February. They have worked closely with the team to get hands-on experience of reporting and have attended all training and mentoring sessions provided to Bilan while they have been with the team.
Reporting standards have steadily improved. Indicators of this include: (a) External validation from some of the world’s biggest media houses. Content has been commissioned from Bilan from the Guardian, BBC and El Pais. In addition, the first report from El Pais has been translated and used on their English as well as Spanish sites, which they only do for their best reports. (b) Audience numbers on social media continue to rise and far outperform comparable journalism from Bilan’s male peers, with the most compelling reports getting over 275,000 views each – such as the recent piece on HIV. (c) Informal feedback from internal and external audiences, including journalism peers, government figures, embassy staff, the general public (both online and through calls to the Bilan offices) and organisations working to support journalists are all positive, with praise for Bilan’s reporting and the way it is changing the face of Somali media. Bilan have been invited to attend events ranging from consultations at the OPM and UN Embassy to trainings with local media associations. Some of these external endorsements can be seen throughout Bilan’s website: www.bilan.media (d) Additional video/radio editing support that was brought on in May has been discontinued because Bilan no longer need it.
Targets: Reports appear weekly on local media and at least one report is picked up internationally per quarter
Bilan have noted they are now able to produce quality reports, videos and short stories since joining the program and receiving trainings from renowned journalists. The women journalists highlighted the importance of programs such as SWoMP in increasing the voice of women in society through women-led journalism and community engagements.
Bilan have produced more than 70 reports, including 7 for international media. Reports go out locally once or twice a week. A list of most reports with titles, links and publications dates/locations is available here (note that this does not include several pieces – such as reporting from COP27 – that went straight into Dalsan’s existing TV or radio packages with no social media link)
